title: Look up — the cross, and where London starts
learning_goal: Find two things without being told where to point: the 1865 replica cross overhead, and the direction of the Charles I statue — the point London's distances are measured from.

narration.script: Stop here. Two things to find. The first is straight above you: follow the cross up to its very top, twenty-one metres, seventy feet, of Portland stone. It is a replica, put up in 1865 — the year the hotel behind it opened. The second is harder. Turn to your right, out of the forecourt, and look about two hundred metres towards Trafalgar Square. You cannot quite see him from here, but King Charles the First rides there in bronze. The first cross, of 1291, stood on that spot — and London still measures its distances from him, not from the stone above your head.

variants.clear: Stop here. Two things to find. The first is straight above you: follow the cross up to its top — twenty-one metres, seventy feet, of stone. It is a copy, put up in 1865 — the year the hotel behind it opened. The second is harder. Turn to your right, out of the station yard, and look about two hundred metres towards Trafalgar Square. You cannot quite see him from here, but a statue of King Charles the First rides there. The first cross, from 1291, stood on that spot. London still measures its distances from that statue, not from the stone above your head.

interaction.prompt: Two things to find: the top of the cross above you, then the way towards Charles I — drag the view to look.

production_notes: STOP-AND-LOOK (D6). The chapter's one Street View stop, and the only scene that asks the traveller to aim their own gaze. Player: Maps **Embed** (drag to look) — free SKU, no programmatic camera needed, no billable call; the `camera` cues are the guided version and dragging pauses them for 4 s (player v0.4). Two finds, both said out loud: the cross overhead (21 m / 70 ft, replica of 1865, F-21) and the direction of the Charles I statue (≈ 205 m WSW, bearing 229°, F-39 / F-21 note) from which London's distances are measured. The statue is behind buildings from this pano, so its pin stays a plain corner pin with no geo and the script says so. `interaction.kind: look` with a 30-second budget: the traveller looks for as long as they like and the runtime should hand on when the budget is spent. ENGINE REQUEST (one line, not done here — studio/player/index.html is out of scope for this pass): `tick()`'s `needsInput` test exempts only `walk` on a streetview scene, so today a `look` scene waits for the traveller to press ▶ instead of auto-advancing. Either add `look` to that exemption or make `timeout_s` resolve it. Nothing is lost meanwhile — the traveller can look and move on — but it is a stall, not a design. LINEAR CUT: a slow pan over the same open imagery (`panowalk`, stop 0), the words unchanged; per D6 that is an adaptation, not a downgrade. Next: Quiz B (16), then the dialogue (17) — D4.

A1 scene-developer 2026-08-18: Charles I pin → plain corner pin (geo removed); fallback M-26 on the pano; next → quiz-the-weather (Quiz B now precedes the dialogue, D4). A1 narrator 2026-08-18: 36-word Charles I sentence split into three; ends on 'this cross'. A3n narrator+scene-developer 2026-08-19 (newcomer rewrite): spine already plain — script untouched; clear-English variant added. A4 engine-tools 2026-08-19 (v0.4 cinematic Street View): the stop was pointing at the wrong place — 51.5083,-0.1247 resolves to a pano inside the station concourse (station roof + WHSmith at heading 180, imagery 2024-06, verified against the Street View Static image). Moved to the verified outdoor forecourt pano 51.50855,-0.12543 (imagery 2025-07), 16 m from the cross, which frames cross + hotel exactly as the note describes; Content Preparer to confirm and update M-38. Added a four-cue `camera` track: look up the spire (pitch 32) while the pin is up, turn right 87° to the Charles I statue (OSM 12877095809, 205 m WSW) at 13 s as the narration names him, then settle back. From this pano 'to your right' is geometrically true. Narration and overlays untouched. D6 scene-developer 2026-08-19 (stop-and-look pass, founder's instruction): kept as `streetview` — this is the chapter's one genuine stop-and-look, and D6 says such a stop earns Street View because there is something to FIND. The task is now stated in the narration and in the prompt: (1) the Eleanor Cross straight overhead, followed up to its top; (2) where Charles I rides, about 200 m towards Trafalgar Square, from which London's distances are measured. `interaction.kind` walk → **look** and the single route waypoint removed (a route of one is transport grammar); the stop's coordinates now come from the M-38 media entry, which is the same point and the same index (0) the pano cache is keyed to, so the film's pan is unaffected. Duration 25 → 47 s: the old 25 s had no room for a task, and 47 s is what the two finds cost at ≈ 2.15 w/s. `camera` cues KEPT (their `at_waypoint: 0` markers dropped with the route) and re-timed to the longer scene (0 · 3 look up, held to 19 · 19 turn right, held to 37 · 38 settle back, held to the end — i.e. ≈ 0 / 2.8 / 18 / 36 s of the 44 s rendered scene; the holds butt up against each other so the linear pan never drops back to a travel frame between finds), same verified look_at points. A second pin names the cross itself so both finds are labelled; each pin sits within 3 s of the cue that turns to it. Honest limit kept in the words: the statue is 205 m off and behind buildings, so the script says 'you cannot quite see him from here' and points instead — the find is the direction and the fact, not a claim the traveller will see bronze. LINEAR CUT: the scene is no longer interactive-only. D6 says a film cannot offer a task, so the cut sheet plays the SAME open imagery as a slow pan (visual kind `panowalk`, stop 0 = look-up-the-cross-w00, Mapillary 360°, 2025-08, 44 m at 1.7 m/s — walking pace) and the guide names what the player-traveller would have found for themselves. Fallback if the pano cache is absent: the M-26 still, now carried as a media entry so the sidecar can resolve it.
